answer: The joiner tallies every mortise he cuts and enters each door in his tally book against the house it hangs in. A canyon door bought at a fair fails the tally: at the zenith of the mortise the joint must match the joiner's own chisel, and a fair door sags on its hinges within a month. Forging a door means hiring a joiner, cutting false timber and paying 6,700, and the summit entry in the tally book is read at every market, so a door whose mortises were never tallied is taken down.
